text:
ryan: Customer reported that their SIEM stopped receiving audit events around Mar 2. They say the S3 export exists but most expected objects are missing. escalation: CCing eng-sec and infra.

maya: looking. do we have a reproducer? which customer/org id?

ryan: org 87654. they pasted the export manifest: 
```
> s3://redwood-audit-exports/87654/2026-03-02/manifest.json
{
  "objects": [],
  "record_count": 0
}
```
They expect ~1.2M events for that day.

eva: their support case says they saw a KMS key rotation warning the day before. Support forwarded CloudTrail snippets showing PutKeyPolicy and RotateKey events for alias/rdw/audit/87654.

sergio: possible suspects: forwarder failing to decrypt objects after rotation, or role lost kms:Decrypt. check forwarder logs and S3 object headers for x-amz-key-v2/kms-key-id.

audit-forwarder-bot: forwarder job status for org=87654: last_successful_run=1970009000, last_attempt=1970012000, consecutive_failures=3, last_error="kms:DecryptAccessDenied"

maya: that aligns. can you paste the forwarder error trace?

ryan: from forwarder logs: 
```
2026-03-02T04:12:01Z ERROR forwarder org=87654 export=2026-03-02: failed to decrypt object s3://.../part-00012: AccessDenied: Request had insufficient kms:Decrypt permission for arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789:key/abcd-rotated
	at com.redwood.audit.forwarder.KMSClient.decrypt(KMSClient.java:87)
	at com.redwood.audit.forwarder.Forwarder.process(Forwarder.java:211)
```

sergio: quick check — did the customer or a platform job replace the key and forget to grant the forwarder role? run: 
```
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/rdw/audit/87654 --policy
```
and inspect that the principal arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/redwood-audit-forwarder (or the account's cross-account role) has "kms:Decrypt" and "kms:GenerateDataKey". Also check Grants.

maya: also verify S3 object encryption headers: if objects encrypted with the old key id, after rotation they should still be decryptable if the key policy grants decrypt to forwarder. if key was scheduled for rekeying with re-encrypt to new key and old key deleted, that breaks it.

eve (security-oncall): FYI — retention/visibility question: is there a chance objects were never written? customer insists logs were produced. can we confirm producer side?

ryan: support pulled producer app logs: they show events delivered to audit ingest topic and acknowledgements. timestamps line up. the problem is only in export pipeline after day boundary.

maya: hypothesis: our export job attempted to use KMS key alias that was rotated and the new key policy is missing forwarder permissions, causing export to fail and skip batches. three consecutive failures could have left the manifest empty. we need to: 1) confirm key policy, 2) check forwarder role's permissions in org 87654 (cross-account?), 3) re-run export/backfill or enable replay.

sergio: perms fix if confirmed: update key policy to include the forwarder role and re-run grant creation: 
```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/redwood-audit-forwarder" },
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
then create a temporary grant: 
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/rdw/audit/87654 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/redwood-audit-forwarder --operations Decrypt GenerateDataKey
```

maya: after perms fixed, to backfill we can re-run the export job for that day. note: if old key was scheduled for deletion and material destroyed, we cannot recover — we'd need raw ingest replays (if customers kept producer logs). confirm key status: 
```
aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/rdw/audit/87654
```
look for "KeyState": "PendingDeletion" or "Disabled".

eva: customer says they did rotate via console and believed rotation is safe. can we provide steps/status and ETA to restore events?

ryan: plan I suggested to them: 1) infra will confirm key policy & grants (sergio). 2) if perms-only issue, we'll apply grant and re-run export for 2026-03-02 and share a temporary S3 manifest. 3) if key material destroyed, we will coordinate replay options and offer retention exception windows while backfill runs.

security-oncall: add compliance note — if replays include PII, ensure replay job runs in private env and that KMS/HSM keys used for re-encrypt meet org's retention policy. log an internal ticket for audit trail (REDW-1882).

sergio: checking now, saw that the key exists but policy replaced by admin user during rotation. missing forwarder role. I created a grant (grant id g-0a1b2c) and re-run export attempt at 1970015000.

audit-forwarder-bot: rerun report: export attempt for org=87654 on 2026-03-02: success. uploaded 1,210,432 objects, manifest updated.

ryan: forwarding to customer: "we found the KMS policy change removed the forwarder principal. we've applied a temporary grant and re-ran the export; your SIEM manifest now contains the expected objects. we'll follow up with a permanent policy change recommendation and a runbook for rotation. apologies for the outage." :white_check_mark:

eva: customer acknowledged and asked for a summary of root cause + steps to avoid. i'll draft the customer-facing note after we finalize internal runbook.

maya: internal followups: - update rotation docs to include forwarder principal checklist - add monitoring alert for forwarder kms:Decrypt errors to PagerDuty - consider auto-grant workflow when rotation detected

ryan: thanks all, marking resolved for now. i'll keep ticket open until runbook published. :)
